chains.title: Alt T strengthens a CEBPA site in the dELS and is associated with higher liver SORT1 and LDL trait

links.claim: CEBPA binds the alt T allele more strongly than ref G at this base. CEBPA has an ENCODE HepG2 ChIP-seq peak over the variant and is highly expressed in DepMap Hep 3B2.1-7; its QBiC-SELEX entry shows alt>ref (z 22.81, effect +2.331, strong alt site). Caveat: the best CEBPA QBiC model is CIS-BP-mapped from CEBPB, and allele-specific occupancy at rs12740374 is not demonstrated.
The variant lies in the active distal enhancer cCRE EH38E1374646 (dELS), with DNase, H3K27ac and H3K4me3 support, so an allele-specific TF change at this base could alter enhancer activity.
The alt T allele is associated with higher SORT1 expression in liver (NES +1.27), and SORT1 has the top L2G score with a liver SQTL signal, supporting SORT1 as a plausible distal target.
The relevant context is liver/hepatocyte: the SORT1 eQTL is in liver, CEBPA is expressed in Hep 3B2.1-7, and ChIP occupancy is in HepG2, a liver cancer line used as a stand-in for Hep 3B2.1-7.

rs12740374 is strongly associated with LDL/high cholesterol, but the direction needs harmonization: the strongest high-cholesterol/LDLC records list G as the effect/risk allele at risk-allele frequency ~0.78, while one LDL record lists T. Alt T is associated with higher liver SORT1, but the provided evidence does not directly show that changing SORT1 expression causally changes LDL or MI risk.

predictions: Allele-specific CEBPA ChIP or reporter activity is higher on alt T than ref G in hepatocytes.
CEBPA knockdown/CRISPRi reduces the alt-T-associated enhancer activity and SORT1 expression.
CEBPB does not show stronger allele-specific occupancy than CEBPA at this base.
falsified_if: CEBPA does not bind allele-specifically at this base in hepatocytes.
CEBPA loss does not change the alt-T enhancer effect or SORT1 expression.
CEBPB, not CEBPA, explains the allele-specific C/EBP-family occupancy.

chains.title: Alt T strengthens a CEBPB site in the dELS and is associated with higher liver SORT1 and LDL trait

links.claim: CEBPB binds the alt T allele more strongly than ref G in vitro: its own QBiC-SELEX model gives z 22.81, effect +2.331 and a strong alt site. CEBPB occupancy at this exact base in HepG2 is not explicitly reported in the provided evidence, although E04 shows broad HepG2 TF occupancy over the variant; this occupancy link is therefore plausible but less directly supported than for CEBPA.
The variant lies in the active dELS EH38E1374646, so a CEBPB binding change at this base could alter enhancer output.
The alt T allele is associated with higher SORT1 expression in liver (NES +1.27), and SORT1 has the top L2G score with a liver SQTL signal, making SORT1 a plausible target of this element.

The candidate context is liver/hepatocyte: the SORT1 eQTL is in liver, E04 reports broad HepG2 occupancy, and CEBPB is a liver-expressed C/EBP-family factor, though no primary hepatocyte CEBPB ChIP is provided.

rs12740374 is strongly associated with LDL/high cholesterol, but the effect-allele direction is not fully harmonized in E15, and no provided experiment shows that CEBPB-dependent SORT1 change causally alters LDL or MI risk.

predictions: Allele-specific CEBPB ChIP is stronger on alt T than ref G in hepatocytes.
CEBPB knockdown/CRISPRi reduces the alt-T enhancer effect and SORT1 expression.
CEBPA does not show stronger allele-specific occupancy than CEBPB at this base.
falsified_if: CEBPB does not occupy this base allele-specifically in hepatocytes.
CEBPB loss does not affect the alt-T enhancer or SORT1 expression.
CEBPA, not CEBPB, explains the C/EBP-family allele-specific signal.

chains.title: Alt T strengthens a CEBPG site in the same enhancer and is associated with higher liver SORT1

links.claim: CEBPG binds the alt T allele more strongly than ref G. CEBPG has its own QBiC-SELEX model with a strong alt-specific effect (z 26.76, effect +2.321), is expressed in Hep 3B2.1-7, and has an ENCODE HepG2 ChIP-seq peak over the variant. C/EBP paralogs share binding specificity, so CEBPG is a candidate but not uniquely resolved.
The variant is in the active dELS EH38E1374646, consistent with CEBPG acting through this enhancer.
The alt T allele is associated with higher SORT1 mRNA in liver, and SORT1 is the top L2G gene, so CEBPG binding could increase SORT1 expression.
CEBPG is expressed in Hep 3B2.1-7, ChIP occupancy is in HepG2, and the SORT1 eQTL is in liver, supporting a liver context with cancer-line caveats.
Alt T is associated with higher liver SORT1 and with LDL/high-cholesterol GWAS signals, but the effect-allele direction needs harmonization and SORT1-to-LDL causality is not shown here.

CEBPA and CEBPB do not show stronger allele-specific occupancy than CEBPG.

CEBPG loss does not affect the SORT1 eQTL or enhancer activity.
Another C/EBP paralog fully explains the allele-specific signal.

chains.title: Alt T strengthens a CEBPA site and is associated with higher CELSR2, with CELSR2 contributing to the LDL trait

links.claim: CEBPA binds the alt T allele more strongly, supported by its HepG2 ChIP occupancy over the variant and its QBiC-SELEX alt-specific increase, with the same caveat that the best CEBPA model is CIS-BP-mapped from CEBPB and allele-specific occupancy is not demonstrated.
The variant is in the dELS EH38E1374646 and also overlaps the CELSR2 3_prime_UTR, so this element or the transcript overlap could regulate CELSR2 in addition to distal genes.
The alt T allele is associated with higher CELSR2 expression in liver (NES +1.04), and CELSR2 has high L2G support (0.98), making CELSR2 a plausible target.
The relevant context is liver/hepatocyte: the CELSR2 liver eQTL is present, CEBPA is expressed in Hep 3B2.1-7, and ChIP is in HepG2.

rs12740374 is strongly associated with LDL/high cholesterol, and alt T is associated with higher CELSR2, but the CELSR2-to-LDL causal direction is not shown, and target-gene ambiguity remains because SORT1 has equally strong L2G support.

predictions: Allele-specific CEBPA binding tracks CELSR2 expression more closely than SORT1 expression in some liver contexts.
CEBPA site disruption reduces the CELSR2 eQTL effect.
CELSR2, not SORT1, mediates part of the phenotype in the relevant hepatocyte state.
falsified_if: CELSR2 expression is not affected by the CEBPA site.
SORT1 fully explains the LDL effect and CELSR2 has no independent contribution.
The CELSR2 signal is explained by the 3_prime_UTR transcript overlap rather than enhancer regulation.

grades_v0.reason: E21 gives CEBPA QBiC-SELEX alt>ref (z 22.81, effect +2.331) with a strong alt site, and reports an ENCODE HepG2 ChIP-seq peak over the variant; E04 confirms broad occupancy. Caveat: the best QBiC model is CIS-BP-mapped from CEBPB, not CEBPA's own model.
E03 and E01 place the variant in the active dELS EH38E1374646 with DNase, H3K27ac and H3K4me3 support.
E17 shows the alt T allele associated with higher SORT1 in liver (NES +1.27), and E16 gives SORT1 the top L2G score and a liver SQTL PIP of 0.72.
GTEx liver eQTL supports liver context; CEBPA is expressed in Hep 3B2.1-7 and ChIP is in HepG2, though HepG2 is a cancer-line stand-in.

E15 gives strong LDL/high-cholesterol GWAS association, but the SORT1-to-LDL causal step is not experimentally shown. E15 also has mixed effect-allele reporting, including an LDL record with effect allele T, so the alt-T non-risk direction needs harmonization.
E20 gives CEBPG's own QBiC-SELEX model with alt>ref (z 26.76, effect +2.321) and an ENCODE HepG2 ChIP-seq peak over the variant; E04 confirms occupancy.
E03/E01 place the variant in the active dELS EH38E1374646.
E17 and E16 support higher SORT1 with alt T and top L2G/SQTL evidence for SORT1.
CEBPG expression in Hep 3B2.1-7, HepG2 ChIP occupancy, and liver SORT1 eQTL support a liver context, with cancer-line caveats.
GWAS association is strong but no CEBPG/SORT1 perturbation links the enhancer allele to LDL; direction also depends on harmonizing E15 effect alleles.
Same CEBPA occupancy plus QBiC-SELEX alt>ref evidence as H1, with the same caveat that the best QBiC model is CIS-BP-mapped from CEBPB.
E03/E01 show the variant in dELS EH38E1374646 and in the CELSR2 3' UTR; the overlap is direct, though enhancer-to-CELSR2 regulation is not proven.
E17 shows alt T associated with higher CELSR2 in liver (NES +1.04), and E16 gives CELSR2 high L2G support (0.98) plus CELSR2 eQTL/tuQTL signals.
Liver CELSR2 eQTL, CEBPA expression in Hep 3B2.1-7, and HepG2 ChIP support liver context, again with cancer-line stand-in caveats.
The variant-phenotype association is strong, but CELSR2-to-LDL causality is not shown; the chain itself notes this link is less supported than SORT1.
E22 gives MLX QBiC-SELEX ref>alt (z -15.37, effect -0.496) with a strong ref site and an ENCODE HepG2 ChIP-seq peak over the variant.
E03/E01 show an active dELS, but they do not show that MLX is a repressor at this element or that losing its site increases enhancer output.
E17 supports alt T associated with higher SORT1 in liver, but there is no evidence that MLX represses this element or that MLX loss increases SORT1; the derepression mechanism is inferred.
MLX is expressed in Hep 3B2.1-7, has HepG2 ChIP occupancy over the variant, and the SORT1 eQTL is in liver.
GWAS association is present, but the MLX derepression-to-SORT1-to-LDL chain is not experimentally supported, and allele direction still depends on E15 effect-allele harmonization.

grades_final.reason: Occupancy is present (E21/ENCSR142IGM HepG2 ChIP peak over the variant) and a QBiC-SELEX change in the stated direction is reported (z 22.81, effect +2.331, alt strong site), but the model driving that change is explicitly a CIS-BP-mapped CEBPB model, and E36 shows the identical z/effect for CEBPB's own model — so the allele-specific in vitro change is not CEBPA-specific. Allele-specific occupancy is not demonstrated. The choice of CEBPA over its paralogs is not justified; paralog-proxy caveat flagged.

E03 places this exact variant inside cCRE EH38E1374646 (dELS) with DNase z 4.9, H3K27ac z 4.8, H3K4me3 z 4.2; E01 independently annotates an ENSR enhancer at the site. Caveat: the z-scores are maxima over ENCODE biosamples, not HepG2/liver-specific, so enhancer activity in the relevant cell type is inferred, not shown.

E17 gives a liver eQTL for SORT1 (alt T NES +1.27, p 3.1e-54) — effect of the same allele the chain models — and E16 gives SORT1 L2G 0.99 plus a liver sQTL credible set (PIP 0.72). Genetic (colocalising QTL/L2G) evidence directly ties this variant to SORT1 in liver, despite the 123 kb distance in E02.

Liver eQTL for SORT1 (E17), CEBPA expression 141.33 TPM in DepMap ACH-000625 (E21), and HepG2 ChIP occupancy over the variant (E21/E04) jointly support a hepatocyte/liver-cancer-line context; HepG2/Hep3B2 stand-in is a reasonable but imperfect match.

E15 shows overwhelming association with LDL/high cholesterol, but effect-allele reporting is internally inconsistent (G listed as effect allele at risk-allele frequency ~0.78 for high cholesterol and LDLC in PMID 39024449, while one LDL record lists T), so the sign connecting alt T → higher SORT1 → higher LDL is not established from the supplied evidence. No perturbation data (CRISPR/reporter) causally linking SORT1 to LDL or MI is provided; the chain itself concedes this.

E36 provides a CEBPB own-model QBiC-SELEX change in the stated direction (z 22.81, effect +2.331, alt 99.8th percentile site), which is the stronger form of the in vitro evidence. However no CEBPB ChIP-seq peak over the variant in HepG2 is reported anywhere: E04's explicit C/EBP-family member with a peak here is CEBPA, and CEBPB is not named (only '+100 more'). Occupancy for CEBPB is therefore only indirect — one of the two required pieces is weak.

E03 places the variant in the EH38E1374646 dELS with DNase/H3K27ac/H3K4me3 support and E01 annotates an enhancer; the variant-in-active-element claim is directly shown, though biosample-specific z-scores (liver) are not given.
E17 liver SORT1 eQTL (alt T NES +1.27, p 3.1e-54) and E16 SORT1 L2G 0.99 / liver sQTL PIP 0.72 directly support SORT1 as the target gene for the alt allele in liver.

The liver eQTL (E17) is real, but CEBPB expression in DepMap ACH-000625 is nowhere in the evidence (E36 gives no TPM) and no CEBPB ChIP in HepG2 or hepatocytes is reported; the claim that CEBPB is a liver-expressed C/EBP factor is asserted, not evidenced.

E15 establishes strong LDL/cholesterol association, but effect alleles are not harmonised across records (G vs T) so the direction of effect of alt T is unresolved, and no experiment links a CEBPB-dependent SORT1 change to LDL or MI.

E20 gives CEBPG's own model (not a paralog proxy) with alt>ref (z 26.76, effect +2.321, alt site at 99.4th percentile) and an ENCODE HepG2 ChIP-seq peak over the variant (ENCSR639IIZ) — both required components in the correct direction. Residual caveats: the ChIP peak is not allele-specific, and the C/EBP paralogs (CEBPA/CEBPB, E21/E36) show the same directional change, so CEBPG is not uniquely the factor; that ambiguity belongs to specificity, not to this link's support.
E03 (dELS EH38E1374646 containing the variant, DNase 4.9/H3K27ac 4.8/H3K4me3 4.2) and E01 enhancer annotation directly support the element claim; biosample specificity of the marks is not shown.
E17 liver SORT1 eQTL with alt T increasing expression (NES +1.27) and E16 SORT1 L2G 0.99 with a liver sQTL credible set (PIP 0.72) support SORT1 as target.
CEBPG is expressed at 46.37 TPM in DepMap ACH-000625 (E20), has HepG2 occupancy over the variant (E20/E04), and the SORT1 eQTL is in liver (E17); the cancer-line stand-in caveat is acknowledged.

E15 gives strong LDL/cholesterol associations but inconsistent effect-allele reporting (G vs T), so alt-T direction toward higher LDL is not demonstrated, and no perturbation evidence connects CEBPG-driven SORT1 change to LDL or MI.

Same defect as H1: occupancy over the variant in HepG2 is documented (E21/ENCSR142IGM), but the QBiC-SELEX change credited to CEBPA comes from a CIS-BP-mapped CEBPB model (E36 shows the identical statistic for CEBPB's own model), so the allele-specific in vitro change is not attributable to CEBPA; allele-specific occupancy unproven and the paralog choice unjustified.

E03 annotates the variant in dELS EH38E1374646 with chromatin marks and E01 confirms both the enhancer and a CELSR2 3_prime_UTR_variant consequence, so both parts of the claim (enhancer and transcript overlap) are directly supported for this variant.

E17 CELSR2 liver eQTL (alt T NES +1.04, p 9.4e-34) and E16 CELSR2 L2G 0.98 give direct genetic support that the alt allele tracks higher CELSR2 in liver; the chain appropriately notes SORT1 has comparable support.

CELSR2 liver eQTL (E17), CEBPA expression in ACH-000625 (E21, 141 TPM) and HepG2 ChIP over the variant (E21/E04) support the liver/hepatocyte context, with the HepG2-for-Hep3B2 substitution as a stated caveat.

E15 supports strong LDL/cholesterol association, but effect-allele direction is unresolved (G at RAF ~0.78 for high cholesterol/LDLC vs T in one LDL record), no causal CELSR2→LDL experiment is cited, and E16's L2G places SORT1 (0.99) at least as high as CELSR2, leaving the effector gene ambiguous — the chain's own caveat is correct.

QBiC-SELEX screen of chr1:109274968:G>T, one line per TF, each with the TF's own or CIS-BP-mapped model of largest |z|. Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap line ACH-000625), bound here before bound elsewhere, then a strong site before a weak one, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 10 of 140 occupied (63 with a strong site), 5 of 78 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 251 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 170 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 12 bound but below 1 TPM. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th. At a weak site the ChIP peak more likely reflects another site in the element.
